messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: GPU-pool-a exhausted (p95 queue depth > 95th percentile). Trigger: gpu-queue-threshold. Affected: hosted-api-us-west. Escalation: oncall infra -> marie.

marie: acknowledged — I'm on it. pulling up dashboard now.

kevin: aware. seeing HPA not reacting for ~8m, kube-metrics-server shows scrape errors. Prom adapter 502s in logs.

sophia: Prometheus adapter error bursts started ~1795054800. adapter->kube_api 504s, backlog in custom-metrics queue.

marie: customer-impact check: Status page shows increased 504s for text-generation endpoints, some requests getting queued for >10s. CS bot reports 3 customer tickets with latency spike.

customer-success-bot: Ticket #CR-4821: enterprise customer "Clearbank" intermittent failures, many calls time out after 15s. They reported at 18:12 PST.

jordan: gpu-queue length: 210 -> capacity is 64 GPUs; pods pending due to not scaling. Autoscaler logs: "no new replicas created: metrics not available".

eli: quick mitigation idea: manually scale up Dedicated pool to handle immediate backlog, then rollback once metrics pipeline fixed. Anyone object?

kevin: +1 manual scale. but note: if adapter still broken the HPA wont observe new metrics; we need to avoid flapping. Suggest add 20% headroom and enable fallback routing to small-llm-quantized variant.

sophia: investigating Prom adapter: saw memory spike then OOM in adapter-0 and adapter-1. Restarting adapter replicas now.

marie: doing live mitigation steps: 1) trigger manual scale to add 12 GPUs 2) restart prometheus-adapter 3) enable fallback model routing 4) notify CS.

kevin: commands I'm running:
```
# scale nodepool (cloud API)
# internal infra tool
infractl scale pool gpu-pool-a --add 12
# scale deployment as immediate fallback (k8s)
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/gpu-inference --replicas=100
```
Note: kubectl scale will create pods but if cluster autoscaler blocked will still pend. infractl should create nodes.

sophia: prometheus-adapter restarts done. adapter logs show start, but still 503 to kube api for a bit. increasing log level to debug for next 10m.

marie: routing change in progress: enabling route rule to fallback small-llm-quantized for low-priority traffic. Doing a canary 10% first.

jordan: queue depth dropped to 120 after scaling actions. Some pending still. Throttling rules active: token-bucket throttles are firing to protect infra.

eli: FYI customers on Dedicated unaffected; hosted customers seeing degraded throughput.

kevin: also noticed custom metric "gpu_pool_utilization" values delayed by ~30s due to long scrape time. HPA window is 60s so borderline. Need to clear backlog.

marie: CS notified customers (standard incident template) with initial impact note and mitigations underway.

customer-success-bot: Sent update to affected customers at 18:22 PST.

oncall-system: automated handoff scheduled in 50m. Marie — are you taking the handoff?

marie: I'll take the handoff for next 30m then pass to kevin for followthrough. leaving notes in the incident doc.

kevin: digging into metrics pipeline: prometheus remote write queue large due to remote cluster flapping. adapter pulls from Prom; when remote-write backlog grows adapter CPU spikes. Suggest temporarily disable remote-write to reduce adapter load. Opinions?

sophia: disabling remote-write reduces ingestion pressure but we must ensure no data loss for compliance; remote-write retention policy will keep buffer for 2h. I support temporary disable for 15m.

eli: manual ops approved. I'll flip remote-write off, monitor for adapter recovery.

kevin: after remote-write disabled adapter error rate dropped from 18%->2% and custom metrics backlog decreased. HPA started scaling again.

jordan: observed new replicas provisioning and GPU pool utilization moving down. queue depth now ~32. Request latency for affected endpoints improving.

marie: good. move to mitigation->recovery: we should leave small-llm fallback rule enabled for another 20m while we watch for regressions.

sophia: adding postmortem note: root cause looks like combination of remote-write surge causing adapter OOM and metrics-server scrape timeouts which together prevented HPA from seeing metrics and triggered scale lag. We'll capture exact sequence + timeline.

customer-success-bot: Sent update to customers at 18:38 PST: "We have restored capacity and are monitoring. Some requests may still be routed to quantized fallback."

marie: quick checklist for handoff to kevin: 1) keep prometheus-adapter logs at debug for 30m 2) restore remote-write after stable 15m 3) keep fallback routing at 10% for now 4) watch for CPU/mem on adapter and kube-metrics-server 5) draft incident summary for postmortem.

kevin: taking handoff. I'll be on this. If queue re-grows to >100 reopen paging.

eli: note for follow-up: investigate autoscaler thresholds; consider raising HPA target windows during high ingestion events, and add backpressure signal directly to API to avoid queue growth.

marie: closing slack thread for live mitigation — will file incident ticket and assign action items. Any objections to marking this as "mitigated - monitoring"? :eyes:

jordan: fine from ops side.

sophia: fine, filing PR with prometheus-adapter resource limits and restart policies.

kevin: fine. I'll own postmortem and action list.

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: gpu-pool-a capacity restored, severity downgraded to P2. Metrics: queue depth normalized.

marie: thanks everyone — handing off to kevin for postmortem and retro.
